docs.title: Indicium
docs.text:
The shared standard for typed scientific claims bound to their evidence.

Every claim minted by any tool in the agentic science ecosystem carries its indicia: the typed, provenance-stamped evidence that justifies believing it. Indicium defines the binding — claim → evidence → source — so claims produced by ASTRA, AgenticScienceBuilder (ASB), and Perspicacité are structurally identical and mergeable.

docs.title: Reuse axes
docs.text: Axis Standard Evidence type ECO (Evidence & Conclusion Ontology) Claim ↔ citation relation CiTO Source / document type DoCO + IAO Article type FaBiO Assertion + evidence structure SEPIO Provenance PROV-O Claim structure Bucur et al. 5-slot SuperPattern (K-CAP 2021)

docs.title: What Indicium defines
docs.text: Component What it is Claim 5-slot Bucur SuperPattern (context / subject / qualifier / relation / object) with ECO-typed evidence Evidence A typed, CiTO-linked evidence record grounding a claim Source A DoCO/FaBiO-typed document or artefact that an evidence record points to CitationLink A CiTO-typed directed relation between two claims or between a claim and a source

docs.title: Install
docs.text: pip install indicium

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
from indicium import validate_graph, claim_to_insight
from indicium.adapters.scitask import claim_to_evidence_snippet

claim = {
    "id": "c001",
    "context": "in vitro",
    "subject": "compound A",
    "qualifier": "inhibits",
    "relation": "inhibits growth of",
    "object": "cell line B",
    "source_excerpt": "Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%.",
    "evidence": [{"doi": "10.1234/test"}],
}

# Project to SciTask EvidenceSnippet
snip = claim_to_evidence_snippet(claim)

# Project to ASTRA Insight
insight = claim_to_insight(claim)

docs.title: The name
docs.text: Indicium (Latin) is "a sign or mark that points to the truth" — in law, the evidentiary indication. Every claim carries its indicia, the traces that justify believing it.

docs.title: indicium.adapters.astra
docs.text:
Project an indicium Claim onto an ASTRA Insight (lossy — claim becomes a string).

ASTRA Insight = {id, claim (str), evidence: [{doi|artifact, quote:{exact}}]}. The 5-slot SuperPattern is flattened into the claim string; full typing is preserved in the RDF/RO-Crate forms, not here.

docs.title: indicium.adapters.kgmemory
docs.text:
KGmemory-ready projection (latent). Points outward at mem:SemanticMemory.

We do NOT import, vendor, or modify KGmemory's vocabulary — we only reference its canonical IRI so an emitted claim is ingestible if/when KGmemory adopts it. The ECO->validationState crosswalk is intentionally NOT here (it is KGmemory's seam to author).

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
Schema and package version history for Indicium.

Versions follow Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Indicium 1.0.0 — 2026-05-23
docs.text: First stable public release.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Core schema (src/indicium/schema/indicium.yaml) — Claim (Bucur 5-slot SuperPattern), Evidence (ECO-typed), Source (DoCO/FaBiO-typed), CitationLink (CiTO-typed), with SEPIO assertion structure and PROV-O provenance.
  • Generated artefacts — Pydantic v2 model (model.py), SHACL shapes (shapes.ttl), OWL ontology (ontology.ttl), JSON Schema (schema.json).
  • SHACL validation — validate_graph() via pyshacl over generated + supplemental shapes.
  • ASTRA adapter — claim_to_insight() projects a Claim to an ASTRA Insight.
  • SciTask adapter — claim_to_evidence_snippet() projects a Claim to a SciTask EvidenceSnippet (new in this release).
  • KGmemory adapter — claim_jsonld() emits a JSON-LD node referencing the KGmemory namespace (latent; documentation deferred).
  • IRI bindings — iri_bindings.py with canonical ECO/CiTO/DoCO/IAO IRIs.
  • Public API — validate_graph, claim_to_insight, claim_to_evidence_snippet, claim_jsonld, MEM_NS exported from indicium.
  • Spec site — MkDocs Material site deployed to GitHub Pages (holobiomicslab.github.io/indicium).
  • GitHub Actions — docs.yml (site deploy on push to main), release.yml (GitHub Release + artefact upload on tag).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install indicium
# or with uv:
uv add indicium

For codegen (regenerating pydantic model / SHACL / OWL from the LinkML source):

pip install indicium[codegen]

docs.title: The claim dict format
docs.text:
Indicium adapters consume a claim dict — a plain Python dictionary with the following keys:

Key Required Type Notes id yes str Stable identifier (e.g. "c001", a UUID, or a URN) context yes str Experimental or conceptual setting subject yes str Entity the claim is about qualifier yes str One of the 20 Bucur SuperPattern terms relation yes str Free-text elaboration of the relation object yes str Target entity claim_type no str "explicit" or "implicit" source_excerpt no str Verbatim text from the source evidence no list[dict] Each item may carry doi, artifact, quote, evidence_type

The formal Claim Pydantic model (indicium.generated.model.Claim) validates the same required slots and the qualifier enum, and produces a compatible dict via .model_dump(). The evidence list is an adapter-layer convenience; in the RDF/SHACL model, evidence is a separate Evidence class linked to a claim via for_claim.

docs.title: Round-trip example
docs.text:
from indicium import validate_graph, claim_to_insight, claim_to_evidence_snippet

claim = {
    "id": "c001",
    "context": "in vitro",
    "subject": "compound A",
    "qualifier": "inhibits",
    "relation": "inhibits growth of",
    "object": "cell line B",
    "source_excerpt": "Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%.",
    "evidence": [
        {
            "doi": "10.1234/test",
            "quote": "Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%.",
            "evidence_type": "data",
        }
    ],
}

# Project to ASTRA Insight (for astra validate)
insight = claim_to_insight(claim)
print(insight)
# {'id': 'c001', 'claim': 'compound A inhibits growth of cell line B (in vitro)',
#  'evidence': [{'doi': '10.1234/test', 'quote': {'exact': 'Compound A ...'}}]}

# Project to SciTask EvidenceSnippet (for ASB SciTask Cards)
snip = claim_to_evidence_snippet(claim)
print(snip)
# {'snippet_id': 'c001', 'source_path': 'doi:10.1234/test',
#  'reason': 'compound A [inhibits] inhibits growth of cell line B (context: in vitro)',
#  'text': 'Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%.'}

docs.title: SHACL validation
docs.text:
import rdflib
from indicium import validate_graph

g = rdflib.Graph()
g.parse("my_claims.ttl", format="turtle")

conforms, report = validate_graph(g)
if not conforms:
    print(report)

docs.title: Regenerate schema artefacts
docs.text:
cd path/to/indicium
uv sync --extra codegen
make gen

This regenerates src/indicium/generated/model.py, shapes.ttl, ontology.ttl, schema.json from the LinkML source at src/indicium/schema/indicium.yaml.

docs.title: ASTRA Adapter
docs.text: Projects an Indicium Claim dict onto an ASTRA Insight dict.

docs.title: Function
docs.text:
from indicium.adapters.astra import claim_to_insight

insight = claim_to_insight(claim)

The 5-slot SuperPattern is flattened into a single claim string. Evidence records map to ASTRA evidence entries (doi or artifact + optional quote). This is a lossy projection — full typing is preserved in the RDF/RO-Crate forms.

docs.title: Mapping
docs.text: ASTRA field Indicium source id claim["id"] claim "{subject} {relation} {object} ({context})" evidence[].doi evidence[].doi evidence[].artifact evidence[].artifact evidence[].quote.exact evidence[].quote

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from indicium.adapters.astra import claim_to_insight

claim = {
    "id": "c001",
    "context": "in vitro",
    "subject": "compound A",
    "qualifier": "inhibits",
    "relation": "inhibits growth of",
    "object": "cell line B",
    "evidence": [{"doi": "10.1234/x", "quote": "A inhibited B by 80%."}],
}

insight = claim_to_insight(claim)
# {
#   "id": "c001",
#   "claim": "compound A inhibits growth of cell line B (in vitro)",
#   "evidence": [{"doi": "10.1234/x", "quote": {"exact": "A inhibited B by 80%."}}]
# }

docs.title: KGmemory Adapter
docs.text:
In preparation

The KGmemory adapter documentation will be published here when the KGmemory standard is publicly released.

A claim_jsonld() adapter for KGmemory is implemented in src/indicium/adapters/kgmemory.py and ships with this package. It emits a JSON-LD node referencing the KGmemory namespace (http://kgmemory.org/ns#SemanticMemory) so an Indicium claim is ingestible when KGmemory adopts the vocabulary.

docs.title: SciTask Adapter
docs.text: Projects an Indicium Claim dict onto a SciTask Standard EvidenceSnippet dict — the structure embedded in SciTask Cards by AgenticScienceBuilder (ASB).

docs.title: Function
docs.text:
from indicium.adapters.scitask import claim_to_evidence_snippet

snip = claim_to_evidence_snippet(claim)
# or with an explicit source path:
snip = claim_to_evidence_snippet(claim, source_path="results/fig1.png")

docs.title: Mapping
docs.text: SciTask field Indicium source snippet_id claim["id"] source_path First evidence[].artifact, then "doi:<doi>", then "" reason "{subject} [{qualifier}] {relation} {object} (context: {context})" text claim["source_excerpt"], then first evidence[].quote, then ""

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from indicium.adapters.scitask import claim_to_evidence_snippet

claim = {
    "id": "c001",
    "context": "in vitro",
    "subject": "compound A",
    "qualifier": "inhibits",
    "relation": "inhibits growth of",
    "object": "cell line B",
    "source_excerpt": "Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%.",
    "evidence": [{"doi": "10.1234/x", "artifact": "results/fig1.png"}],
}

snip = claim_to_evidence_snippet(claim)
# {
#   "snippet_id": "c001",
#   "source_path": "results/fig1.png",
#   "reason": "compound A [inhibits] inhibits growth of cell line B (context: in vitro)",
#   "text": "Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%."
# }

docs.title: Schema Overview
docs.text:
The Indicium schema has one LinkML source of truth: src/indicium/schema/indicium.yaml

From it, four artefacts are generated:

Artefact Purpose generated/model.py Pydantic v2 models for Python consumers generated/schema.json JSON Schema for any language generated/shapes.ttl SHACL shapes for RDF validation generated/ontology.ttl OWL ontology for semantic alignment

docs.title: Core classes
docs.text:
Claim
 └── evidence: list[Evidence]
      └── of_source: Source

CitationLink   (connects two Claims or a Claim to a Source)

docs.title: The binding
docs.text: The one thing Indicium mints is the binding: a claim → typed evidence → a source, provenance-stamped. The claim structure is borrowed from Bucur et al.; the value Indicium standardizes is the typed grounding of claims in evidence.

docs.title: Claim
docs.text: A scientific claim expressed using the Bucur et al. (K-CAP 2021) 5-slot SuperPattern.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text: Slot Required Ontology Description id yes dct:identifier Stable claim identifier (string, UUID, or URN) context yes asb:context The experimental or conceptual setting subject yes asb:subject What the claim is about qualifier yes asb:qualifier Directional relation from the 20-term vocabulary relation yes asb:relation Free-text relation elaboration object yes asb:object The target entity claim_type no — explicit or implicit source_excerpt no — Verbatim text from the source

docs.title: SuperPatternQualifier vocabulary
docs.text: 20 terms from Bucur et al.: causes, prevents, inhibits, activates, increases, decreases, correlates_with, is_associated_with, predicts, interacts_with, produces, requires, enables, treats, enhances, reduces, has_property, is_part_of, is_a, consistent_with.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
claim = {
    "id": "c001",
    "context": "in vitro",
    "subject": "compound A",
    "qualifier": "inhibits",
    "relation": "inhibits growth of",
    "object": "cell line B",
    "claim_type": "explicit",
    "source_excerpt": "Compound A inhibited cell line B by 80%.",
}

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
An Evidence record grounds a Claim in a typed source.

Slot Required Ontology Description evidence_type no ECO Type of evidence (see table below) source_type no DoCO/IAO Type of source document or artefact quote no — Verbatim passage from the source confidence no — Float 0–1 of_source no — The Source this evidence points to for_claim no — The Claim this evidence grounds

docs.title: EvidenceType (ECO-mapped)
docs.text: Value ECO IRI data ECO:0000006 citation ECO:0000033 knowledge ECO:0000302 inference ECO:0000361 speculation ECO:0000034

docs.title: SourceType (DoCO/IAO-mapped)
docs.text: Value IRI text IAO:0000311 figure doco:Figure table doco:Table image IAO:0000536

docs.title: CitationLink
docs.text:
A CiTO-typed directed relation between a claim and another claim or source.

Slot Ontology Description link_type CiTO Relation type (see table below)

docs.title: LinkType (CiTO-mapped)
docs.text: Value CiTO IRI supports cito:supports disputes cito:disputes qualifies cito:qualifies citesForInformation cito:citesForInformation

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
A Source is a DoCO/FaBiO-typed document or artefact that an Evidence record points to.

Slot Required Ontology Description identifier yes dct:identifier DOI, URL, or local path title no dct:title Human-readable title authors no — List of author names license_id no — SPDX license identifier

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
source = {
    "identifier": "10.1234/test",
    "title": "Inhibition study of compound A",
    "authors": ["Smith J", "Doe A"],
}
